title: Research: F2-right-vector diagonal minimum is the non-identity count (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For every algebra `R` over `F₂` and every finite register count `n`, a product of factors `I + u yᵀ` with `u ∈ Rⁿ` and `y ∈ F₂ⁿ` equals a diagonal matrix only if the number of factors is at least `t`, the number of diagonal entries different from `1`. The coordinate factors `I + (dᵢ − 1) eᵢ eᵢᵀ` attain `t`. The same count is exact for every finite group under the narrower legal alphabet `I + (g − 1) x yᵀ`, including nonabelian groups and labels in `1 + m²`. Commutativity is not used.

The `F₂` restriction on the right vector is sharp. Over `F₂[z₁, z₂]/(z₁², z₂²)`, the single outer product

```text
(z₁, z₂)ᵀ (z₂, z₁) = diag(z₁ z₂, z₁ z₂)
```

gives `diag(1 + z₁ z₂, 1 + z₁ z₂)`. Both diagonal entries differ from `1`, so `t = 2` in one factor, and the right vector is not `F₂`-valued.

[#4098](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4098) is the elementary-abelian special case of this column expansion: restrict to `R = F₂[(C₂)^k]`, `k ≥ 2`, and to `I + (g − 1) x yᵀ`. The argument here is the `F₂`-column expansion in `Rⁿ`, not the graded image in `m/m²`. It also covers noncommutative and infinite algebras, and labels in `1 + m²` that the graded quotient cannot see.

Merged [#2513](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2513) does not imply this statement. Its column lemma is the socle bound for `R = F₂[z]/(z^q)` and its product theorem allows `R`-valued right vectors. The sharpness witness above is not that note's socle column `U = (x, y)ᵀ`.

The Klein enumeration (1,049,600 words) and the `S₃` enumeration (19,740 words) are controls. **No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`. Free `GLₙ(F₂)` changes of basis are not part of the alphabet.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum/`
- Tip: `eb98e998903f6034ac7cc8707bfbd922f7c82cfb`
- Base: `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f`
- Scope: **refined** — all-algebra diagonal minimum for `F₂`-valued right vectors

Closest priors: [#4098](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4098) (PROOF exact shared lines 3/29, token multiset ≈0.46, sequence ≈0.13) and [#2513](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2513) (PROOF exact shared lines 0, token multiset ≈0.32). Shared verify names are `need`, `load_json`, and `diagonal_count`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -O -B -W error research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B -W error research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum/test_verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_F2_RIGHT_VECTOR_DIAGONAL_MINIMUM klein_words=1049600 s3_words=19740 violations=0 sharp_factors=1 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/f2-right-vector-diagonal-minimum outcome=completed
```

`test_verify.py` runs 8 tests. Its Klein and `S₃` multipliers do not import `verify.py`. Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Credit

Credit [#2513](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2513) (`research/bit-cyclic-root-barrier`) for the chain-ring socle theorem and the Klein socle witness, and `research/bit-one-relation-any-registers` for the torsion-free boundary. [#4098](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4098) is the elementary-abelian special case. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions / limitations

1. Do free `GLₙ(F₂)` changes of basis between paid factors realize a diagonal with fewer than `t` factors? The column argument evaluates `P − I` on the standard basis, so a basis change can move the endpoint out of that coordinate frame.
2. Native frame, hosting, and precision bills remain unpriced.
